'''Corvid''' (file extension <code>.cxc</code>) is a language for the Apple ecosystem based on lifecycles. The compiler is written in Clojure, reads <code>.cxc</code>, emits Objective-C, and drives clang to produce macOS binaries.

Programs are a graph of ''atoms'', each owning state and running a lifecycle state machine. Message-triggered transitions replace imperative control flow; iteration is a self-sent message threading state through a Cursor record. There is no <code>while</code>, no <code>for</code>, and no shared-mutable state across atom boundaries. Functional (codata) object-oriented programming without imperative baggage.
